paper.title_en: Exponential <math display="inline"><mrow><mi>U</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> Symmetry-Breaking Phase as a Disorder-Free Quantum Glass
paper.abstract_en: We study the phase diagram of a one-dimensional spin quantum breakdown model, which has an exponential <math display="inline"><mi>U</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math> symmetry with charge unit decaying as <math display="inline"><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msup></math> with site position <math display="inline"><mi>j</mi></math>. By exact diagonalization and density matrix renormalization group, we show that the model with spin <math display="inline"><mi>S</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>2</mn></math> exhibits an exponential <math display="inline"><mi>U</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math> spontaneous symmetry-breaking (SSB) phase dubbed a quantum breakdown condensate. It exhibits a bulk gap violating the Goldstone theorem and an edge mode only on the left edge if in open boundary condition. In a length <math display="inline"><mi>L</mi></math> lattice, the condensate has <math display="inline"><mrow><mi mathvariant="script">O</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>L</mi></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> number of SSB ground states originating from the <math display="inline"><mi mathvariant="script">O</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>L</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math> number of exponential <math display="inline"><mi>U</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math> charge sectors, leading to a finite entropy density <math display="inline"><mi>ln</mi><mn>2</mn></math>. This enforces a first-order SSB phase transition into this phase, as observed numerically and verified in the large <math display="inline"><mi>S</mi></math> limit on an exactly solvable Rokhsar-Kivelson line. The condensate has an SSB order parameter being the local in-plane spin, which points in angles related by the chaotic Bernoulli (dyadic) map and thus is effectively random. Moreover, we show the condensate exhibits nondecaying local autocorrelations and does not have an off-diagonal long-range order. The quantum breakdown condensate thus behaves as a disorder-free quantum glass and is beyond the existing classifications of phases of matter.
